title: Aviation Ordnance Weapons and Tactics Instructor (MGySgt to Sgt) NMOS (6531, 6541, 6591), DC AVN
raw_text:
6. MOS 6577, Aviation Ordnance Weapons and Tactics Instructor (MGySgt to
Sgt) NMOS (6531, 6541, 6591), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Ordnance Chief, quality assurance safety observer and/or
collateral duty inspector assigned to an organizational, intermediate level
work center or staff billet are subject matter experts (SME) on the tactical
employment of expeditionary aviation ordnance operations. AO WTI Marines
support MAGTF and squadron commanders by maintaining safety and operational
standards, readiness levels and possess the knowledge required to
successfully plan, brief, and execute any technique, tactic or procedure
authorized in our warfighting doctrine. They are intimately familiar with
all aspects of employing an ordnance division/department in any expeditionary
environment or operation. They are experts in forward arming refueling
points/forward operational bases/distributed aircraft operations and
expeditionary advanced based operations concepts.

       b.   Prerequisites.

            (1) Must obtain one of the following:

                (a) Must hold a 6591 MOS.

            (b) Or must be a sergeant or above with a 6531 or 6541 MOS and
must possess, or have previously held, the MCO 8023 qualification/
certification of Quality Assurance/Safety Observer (QA/SO).

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Must successfully complete the MAWTS-1 Expeditionary Ordnance
Course (MEOC) (M14G221).

            (2) Must be certified and approved by squadron commanding officer.

    d. Duties. As an Expeditionary Ordnance subject matter expert, they
must be able to effectively and accurately articulate current and future
capabilities of a unit’s ordnance division/department based on current
structure, manpower and qualifications. Identify potential problems and
solve all issues related to logistical considerations, requirements and
capabilities, execution, potential contingencies and retrograde of all
weapons and personnel while observing and adhering to all orders and
regulations regarding explosive safety. Increase the squadron commander’s
capability and lethality by creating, providing, and briefing innovative
solutions and improvements to plans, minimizing risk and increasing combat
effectiveness. Responsible for providing the most capable and highest
trained ordnance division/department to commanders IOT accomplish any given
task.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

 3143                                                              NAVMC 1200.1L
common_text: Aviation Ordnance MOSs handle Class V(A) ammunition issues from safety to procurement, storage, buildup, delivery, and subsequent aircraft loading and downloading. The OccFld includes both organizational and intermediate maintenance of aircraft weapon systems, aircraft guns, gun pods, aircraft crew-served weapons, bomb racks, missile launchers, and armament weapons support equipment (AWSE). Aviation Ordnance Marines are qualified and certified to handle Class V(A) munitions under current directives. Formal schooling is provided to Marines entering the OccFld. A wide variety of billet assignments are available as shown in the figure later in this entry. Marines entering the OccFld receive MOS 6500, Basic Aviation Ordnance Marine, and attend Aviation Ordnance, Class AO A1 School (N23G3U2) at Pensacola, Fl., with follow-on training at one of several CNATT AO(C) courses, dependent upon anticipated fleet assignment. Upon completion of the applicable AO(C) course, they are designated as either MOS 6531 Aircraft Ordnance Technician or MOS 6541 Aviation Ordnance Systems Technician and are assigned to a T/M/S flying squadron in the case of MOS 6531 or a Marine Aviation Logistics Squadron(MALS)/Station Weapons in the case of MOS 6541.

The OccFld includes both organizational and intermediate maintenance of aircraft weapon systems, aircraft guns, gun pods, aircraft crew-served weapons, bomb racks, missile launchers, and armament weapons support equipment (AWSE).
Maintain and perform safety inspections on equipment and tools.

Ordnance Chief, quality assurance safety observer and/or collateral duty inspector assigned to an organizational, intermediate level work center or staff billet are subject matter experts (SME) on the tactical employment of expeditionary aviation ordnance operations.
Develop defense plans or tactics, using intelligence and other information.

As an Expeditionary Ordnance subject matter expert, they must be able to effectively and accurately articulate current and future capabilities of a unit’s ordnance division/department based on current structure, manpower and qualifications.
Examine work orders and converse with equipment operators to detect equipment problems and to ascertain whether mechanical or human errors contributed to the problems.

Identify potential problems and solve all issues related to logistical considerations, requirements and capabilities, execution, potential contingencies and retrograde of all weapons and personnel while observing and adhering to all orders and regulations regarding explosive safety.
Maintain air-to-ground and point-to-point radio contact with aircraft commanders.
Increase the squadron commander’s capability and lethality by creating, providing, and briefing innovative solutions and improvements to plans, minimizing risk and increasing combat effectiveness.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
